options.tooltip: **Record** reads a NetSuite record type with an optional filter. **SuiteQL** runs an arbitrary SuiteQL query. **Saved Search** runs an existing saved search. **RESTlet** calls a customer-deployed RESTlet script.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: Optional column projection; leave empty for all fields

query_filter.title: Query Filter (q)
query_filter.description: Optional record filter using NetSuite's q syntax

options.tooltip: A NetSuite record-filter expression, e.g. `email CONTAINS "acme"` or `id BETWEEN [100, 200]`. See [Filtering results using the q parameter](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_1545222128.html). Leave empty to extract everything.

enum_titles: Separate child table keyed to parent id
options.tooltip: How to handle record sublists (line items). **Flatten** stores each sublist as a JSON string column on the parent row. **Separate child table** writes each sublist to its own table keyed to the parent id. When Separate child table is chosen, each child table's name tracks the NetSuite sublist name (`<output_table>_<sublistName>`).

A [SuiteQL](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_156257770590.html) query. To filter by the date range below, put the `:date_from` and `:date_to` placeholders in the WHERE clause, e.g. `WHERE lastmodifieddate BETWEEN :date_from AND :date_to`. A single range is issued as-is (no automatic chunking), so narrow the range if it would exceed NetSuite's ~100k-row SuiteQL result ceiling.

date_from.title: Start Date
date_from.description: Start of the date range for the :date_from placeholder

options.tooltip: An absolute date (`2024-01-01`) or a relative expression (`5 days ago`, `2 months ago`). Substituted into the query's `:date_from` placeholder at run time. Leave empty to disable date substitution. If set, the query must contain `:date_from` / `:date_to`.

date_to.title: End Date
date_to.description: End of the date range for the :date_to placeholder

options.tooltip: An absolute date (`2024-03-01`) or a relative expression (`now`, `today`, `yesterday`). Substituted into the query's `:date_to` placeholder at run time. Defaults to `now`.

Define any filters inside the saved search itself — the component runs the search exactly as defined and does not add filtering. See [Defining a Saved Search](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_N611578.html).

search_record_type.title: Search Record Type
search_record_type.description: The saved search's underlying record type

options.tooltip: The record type the saved search is built on — it selects the request type used to run the search. Pick a standard type from the list, or type any other value, including custom record types (`customrecord_*`).

query_params.title: Query Parameters
query_params.description: Optional query parameters as a JSON object

options.tooltip: A JSON object of extra query parameters sent to the RESTlet, e.g. `{"since": "2024-01-01"}`. Must be valid JSON. Leave empty for none. See [RESTlets](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_N2971511.html).
The JSON body sent to the RESTlet on POST/PUT requests. Must be valid JSON (an object or an array). Leave empty for no body.

record_path.title: Record Path
record_path.description: Dotted path to the rows in the response, e.g. data.results

options.tooltip: The dotted path to the array (or object) of records in the RESTlet response, e.g. `data.results`. Leave empty when the records are at the top level of the response.

pagination_cursor_field.title: Pagination Cursor Field
pagination_cursor_field.description: Optional response field holding the next-page cursor

options.tooltip: The response field whose value is passed back as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page. Leave empty when the RESTlet is not paginated.
The number of records fetched per API page. NetSuite's REST/SuiteQL surfaces cap this at 1000; higher values are capped to that maximum.

output_table_name.title: Output Table Name
output_table_name.description: Destination table name; defaults to a name derived from the target

primary_key.title: Primary Key
primary_key.description: Columns that uniquely identify a row

options.tooltip: The column(s) that uniquely identify a row. Load suggestions or type any column name. On an incremental load the table is upserted (deduplicated) on this key; a primary key is required when Load Type is Incremental.

load_type.title: Load Type
load_type.description: How the output table is written to Storage

options.tooltip: **Full load** rewrites the whole table on every run. **Incremental load** upserts the fetched rows into the table by the primary key, keeping rows that are not in the current batch. Incremental requires a primary key.
